title: Cooling specifications — 2.3L EcoBoost
introduction:
I use this reference to match the coolant product, fill capacity, freeze protection, pressure limit or thermostat opening stage to the question at hand. Think of it as the cooling system’s recipe card: ingredients, proportions and temperatures each answer a different question.

Keep original-fluid entries separate from service-fluid entries, and match the product description, part identifier and specification together. Capacities are listed in the table’s paired volume units; mixture percentages are coolant first and distilled water second. Pressure entries distinguish the complete system, relief cap and radiator removed from the vehicle. This page supplies specifications, not draining, filling, coolant-changeover or testing instructions, and it does not establish permission to mix coolant types.

edits.why: These entries identify the original coolant products and their listed fill capacity. I distinguish concentrated from prediluted coolant before reading across the row; the capacity column alone does not tell you how to prepare the mixture.

Read each service product’s description, identifier and specification together. The flushing material is a separate entry, and its dash in the capacity column supplies no quantity. Listing original and service products separately does not explain a changeover process.

Read each coolant-to-distilled-water percentage pair across to its freeze-protection temperature, retaining the displayed temperature unit. The extreme-cold qualifier belongs to its particular row; these entries describe protection at the listed proportions rather than a mixing procedure.

Choose the row by what is being evaluated. The complete-system maximum, relief-cap specification and removed-radiator test pressure have different labels and purposes. Keep the pressure unit attached to the value; this table does not supply the equipment, setup or acceptance method for a pressure test.

The thermostat controls coolant flow through the radiator circuit. Beginning to open and reaching fully open are separate stages, so I compare an observation with the matching stage and temperature unit. These specifications alone do not provide a thermostat test or justify a replacement decision.

editorialRevision.scope: Only inherited power parenthetical removed from title; actual 2.3L EcoBoost qualifier and every other public field retained. Complete 26-unit source, tables, raw text, context, author output and independent verdict read; no source illustrations supplied. Original full review retained.
